questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the arteries?

options.text: The fibrous elements present in the tunica intima and media run circularly
The fibrous elements of the tunica adventitia run longitudinally
Collagen fibers are predominantly present in the tunica media
Collagen fibers are predominantly present in the tunica intima

questions.correctAnswerText: The fibrous elements of the tunica adventitia run longitudinally
questions.explanation: The fibrous elements in the intima and the adventitia (mainly collagen) run longitudinally (i.e., along the length of the vessel), whereas those in the media (elastic tissue or muscle) run circularly. The tunica adventitia consists of connective tissue in which collagen fibres are prominent. This layer prevents undue stretching or distension of the artery. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding elastic arteries?

options.text: They are also known as distributing arteries
The internal elastic lamina is distinct from the tunica media
Smooth muscles are absent in the tunica media
The elastic recoil helps in continuous flow of the blood

questions.correctAnswerText: The elastic recoil helps in continuous flow of the blood
questions.explanation: The elastic recoil of the elastic arteries helps in continuous blood flow. The large elastic arteries distend and recoil during systole and diastole respectively due to abundant elastic tissue. The recoiling acts as an additional force that pushes blood into smaller arteries. So, blood flows continuously through arteries but with some fluctuation in pressure during systole and diastole. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The arterioles present in the spleen divide into a number of straight vessels that are called _____.
questions.explanation: The arterioles present in the spleen divide into a number of straight vessels that are called penicilli. The splenic artery after entering the hilum of the spleen divides into about five branches that enter the organ independently. Each branch divides and subdivides as it travels through the trabecular network. Arterioles arising from this network leave the trabeculae to pass into the inter-trabecular spaces. The spleen is histologically composed of: + White pulp - For some distance, each arteriole is surrounded by a dense sheath of lymphocytes. These lymphocytes constitute the white pulp of the spleen. + Penicilli - The arteriole then divides into a number of straight vessels that are calied,penicill. + Ellipsoid - Each of the penicilli shows a localised thickening of its wall that isvalled an ellipsoid. The ellipsoid consists of concentric lamellae formed by ageyesation of fibroblasts and macrophages. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A mislabeled sample of tissue was sent over to the pathology lab for histopathological examination. On microscopy, a characteristic corpuscle as seen in the image was visualised. Which of the following structures is the sample most likely to be from?
questions.explanation: The sample is most likely to be of the thymus because of the presence of the corpuscle of Hassall as seen in the image above. These are small rounded structures formed from eosinophilic type VI epithelial reticular cells present in the medulla of the thymus. Each corpuscle has a central core formed by degenerated epithelial cells appearing as pink stained hyaline mass. Around this mass, there is a wall formed by concentrically arranged epithelial cells which stain bright pink in H and E staining.
